_comment: Normalisation rules shared by tools/compat-record/normalise.py (records the fixtures) and tests/common/normalise.rs (normalises what Thrust answers). Both implement exactly this, in the same traversal order: object keys sorted, request path, then request body, then response body, per exchange, numbering ids across the whole fixture. tests/parity/normalise-cases.json is the shared self-test. Modelled on the oracle's oracle/normalise.yaml in the Plane fork.

opaque_paths._comment: Exact JSON paths ('.' between keys, '[]' for any array element). A value at one of these is replaced by the token; null stays null. These are values a correct implementation cannot reproduce or that name the deployment, not the API.

opaque_keys._comment: Keys that are opaque wherever they appear, at any depth: values the pin makes at random or from the connection (a rotated token, a random default colour, the address and user agent of the last login). A correct implementation sends some string; null stays null.

header_origin_rewrite._comment: The scheme and authority at the start of these headers name the deployment, not the API: the pin redirects to its WEB_URL, Thrust to its own origin. A relative value is left alone.

_headers_comment: cache-control is not kept: the pin answers /api/instances/ with `private, max-age=<remaining TTL>`, which changes per request.

presigned_url._comment: A presigned object-store URL (the upload URL an asset create returns, the redirect an asset read answers) is a URL that has the `marker` parameter in its query. Such a value, at one of `body_paths` (a JSON path as in opaque_paths) or in one of `headers`, is normalised in this order: (1) the scheme and authority at its start are replaced by `origin_token` (the deployment's object store, not the API); (2) the value of each parameter named in `query_tokens` is replaced by its token (the signature, the signing time, the credential and the lifetime, which a correct implementation cannot reproduce); (3) the parameters are stable-sorted by the text before the first `=` (compared as bytes), because the order a signer writes them in is not the contract; (4) the ids in the result (the workspace and the random part of the object key) are numbered like any other string. Parameter names, the other values with their percent-encoding, the path and a fragment are kept. A value that has no such parameter is not touched by this rule, a Location included (it still gets header_origin_rewrite). Response headers are normalised after the request body and before the response body.
